subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & isolation SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@finpay.com>, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & isolation SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Jennifer 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of needs:
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 250ms for user-facing chat, bursts to 1k rps during batch windows
- Predictable throughput and tight isolation during daytime peak (financial transaction scoring)
- Data residency: US-only, with option for customer-managed keys
- Security: SOC 2 + audit log requirements

Options we discussed: Hosted API (fastest time-to-value), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput/isolation), Private VPC/on-prem (for max control).

Open questions for you (so we can recommend the right deployment):
1) How strict are isolation guarantees required? Is noisy-neighbor risk a showstopper or manageable with priority routing?
2) What are your peak qps patterns (typical vs sustained peak hours)?
3) Any constraints around key management / HSM?

Attachments: I attached a draft SLA/ops summary and a short worksheet (finpay-infra-requirements.xlsx) please fill the peak patterns column when you have a moment.

Proposed next steps:
- You fill the worksheet and send back by EOD Friday
- We'll run an internal alignment (marissa + vivek) and propose recommended deployment and a ballpark pricing + migration plan early next week
- If Dedicated or Private looks required, schedule a follow-up technical call with our infra lead (Vivek)

Thanks, look forward to hearing back.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@finpay.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & isolation SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Priyom 

Thanks for the concise recap that matches our notes. Quick answers below: 

1) Isolation: we require hard isolation for peak processing windows (10am-2pm PST) where batch scoring runs. Noisy-neighbor that causes performance variability during that window is not acceptable. Outside that window, risk is acceptable.
2) Typical qps: 30-50 qps baseline, sustained peaks up to ~700 qps during campaign hours, very short bursts to ~1,200 qps (a few minutes)
3) KMS: we can use cloud KMS, but must be able to rotate keys and have audit export to our SIEM. HSM not strictly required today.

We'll fill out the worksheet today and add some comments.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a p95 SLA during the 10am-2pm window if we go Dedicated? If we go Hosted, what mitigations do you recommend to avoid noisy neighbor during peaks?

Thanks,
Jennifer
Head of ML Platform
FinPay

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & isolation SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks Jennifer, great detail, that helps a lot. A few quick clarifications and what we can do: 

- Dedicated: yes, we can commit to a p95 latency SLO during the reserved window when on Dedicated (we include isolation guarantees via reserved GPU pools and scheduling policies). We'll scope an SLA in the draft PDF attached.

- Hosted mitigations: for Hosted API, we suggest:
  * Priority routing to warmed instances for critical routes
  * Auto-burst to isolated reserved capacity for short spikes (subject to availability)
  * Prefix/KV caching and request shaping to smooth bursts

- Key management: Redwood supports cloud KMS integrations and can export audit logs to your SIEM. We can document rotation cadence and audit endpoints in the SOC package.

Next steps: once we receive the worksheet, Marissa and I will map request patterns to a recommended deployment and produce a cost comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) + a sample SLA for Dedicated. If you're comfortable, I'll loop Vivek to run a short technical session next week to validate isolation boundaries and SLO enforcement.

Attaching: redwood-sla-draft.pdf (draft SLA language / uptime & latency sections).

Best,
Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Jennifer Lee <jennifer.lee@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: deployment mode & isolation SLOs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Priyom / Vivek, looping you both here. Jennifer confirmed the critical window and QPS numbers. Vivek, can you please: 

- Confirm on expected Dedicated pool sizes for 700-1,200 qps bursts and whether we need GPU oversubscription adjustments
- Outline how we enforce isolation boundaries (scheduler, tenant cgroups, network shaping) and telemetry we'll expose for FinPay to demonstrate compliance
- Suggest a draft p95 target and penalty framework we can include in the SLA (keep it realistic but competitive)

Jen / Carlos, we'll follow up with our internal sizing + SLA proposal by Monday. If you're comfortable, we can schedule the tech deep-dive with Vivek for Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
